newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF, Russia disagree on revenue projection - MOF. [CORRECTED 11:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IMF, Russia disagree on revenue projection - MOF. [CORRECTED 11:40 GMT]

text.p: Russia and the International Monetary Fund have not yet agreed on the size of government revenues in 1997 and this could delay payments of Russia's $10 billion credit from the fund, a Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.

"We have not fulfilled some demands of the IMF's monetary programme, including revenues," macroeconomic department head Anton Siluanov told Reuters. "But we do not think this will be a reason for freezing the tranche(of IMF funds)."
"We have proposed an alternative for the revenues adjusted to the realities of this year. The new tranche will depend on whether the IMF board agrees with our variant or not."
The 1997 budget provides for revenues of 404.26 trillion roubles, but government officials have acknowledged this figure is unrealistic.
"The budget is politics," Siluanov said. "What we are talking about with the IMF is real life."
There was no immediate comment from the IMF in Moscow.
Last year the IMF repeatedly delayed paying out tranches of the Extended Fund Facility credit because it was dissatisfied by the level of revenues received by the government.
Although some delayed tranches have now been disbursed, the IMF is currently withholding two tranches of about $650 million in all (corrects from $650 million each).
Siluanov said he hoped the IMF board would approve a new tranche.
The Nezavisimaya Gazeta daily said on Tuesday the latest IMF mission had left Moscow and would not recommend to the IMF board that it should approve a new tranche disbursement.
"Russia remains without its due monthly portion of IMF credit for the third time," the paper said.
